name: Week 27 Legs — Knee Flexion Comes Back (Spotlight: Leg Curl / Nordic + Incline RDL)
description:
**Warmups are baked into each block's notes as a reminder.**

**The squat holds at 80 and depth is the entire assignment.** Stability arrived last time — the falling-over feeling is gone and attention moved to depth on its own. Let it stay there.

**Knee-flexion work comes back.** It has been missing since the last legs day was trimmed. **Check the seated leg curl first — if it has been fixed, take it** (position 5, 90 → 100 → 110) and try it single-leg if it is free. The Nordic curl is the fallback, three sets of five, eccentric only.

**The incline RDL changes lever, not load.** Last time it read 'stamina hard, not load hard' — so the reps come down and a 3s eccentric goes on, which turns it back into a tempo lift instead of an endurance one.

**Hip machines hold at 210 and 290**, with a pin available on the abduction if it is still that controlled.

dayOverview.theme:
Two things drive the day. The squat is settled — 80 is stable, powerful, and no longer frightening, so the only remaining thread is depth in the loaded bottom position, and that gets the whole warmup ramp plus three unhurried working sets. And the posterior chain gets its slot back: the last legs day was deliberately trimmed and knee-flexion work was what fell off, so knee flexion returns as the spotlight alongside a reworked incline RDL. Check the seated leg curl first — it has been broken since W24, and if it is fixed it is the better lift here. The Nordic is the fallback.

The Bulgarian stays out one more week. Squat, leg press and a knee-flexion lift are already a lot for a week with a five-day-old in the house, and Friday has a kettlebell flow with lunges in it. The Bulgarian comes back in W28.

spotlights.why: Knee-flexion work has been absent since this machine broke and the last legs day was trimmed — a coverage gap, not a variety choice. If the machine is fixed, it is the better lift here: it loads progressively, it is safe to push, and it does not leave you sore into Friday. The Nordic is the fallback and gets the same attention.
'Stamina hard, not load hard' is a precise report and it means the sets were long rather than heavy. Fewer reps with a 3s eccentric puts the difficulty back where it belongs.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W28 — Bulgarian split squat returns as spotlight, plus leg press. W29 — squat depth and the hip machines. W30 — calf raise and the RDL again.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: back squat, incline RDL, Nordic curl (if used). Spinal-loaded and eccentric-heavy work where the honest ceiling is the rep where depth shortens or the spine rounds.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: seated leg curl, leg press, calf raise, hip abduction, hip adduction. Machine work where form does not degrade dangerously at the limit.

**Depth is the squat's only open thread.** Stability and reps are settled. The loaded bottom still does not reach the depth you get at bodyweight — that is likely ankle and hip mobility rather than strength, so the warmup ramp matters more than the working sets.
**The left calf read 'oddly hard' last time** with no obvious cause. Second look this week — if it repeats, it is worth naming as a pattern rather than a one-off.

**Check the seated leg curl before defaulting to the Nordic.** The Nordic has been the knee-flexion slot only because the machine broke in W24. If it is fixed, take it — progressive load, safe to push, and far less soreness heading into Friday. The Nordic stays as the fallback, and it is eccentric-only at five reps for a reason.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)
sets.notes: The dead bug is the brace rehearsal for the squat — same ribs-down, low-back-flat position, unloaded. The cross-leg lean is the QL release. Both earn their place on a squat day.

exercises.notes: Slow, full depth. **This is your depth benchmark for the day** — the loaded bottom is chasing this.
30s each side. QL and psoas release.
Big circles, unhurried.
Ankle prep — and the ankle is part of the depth question.
Spine wake-up.
Deep core before anything loaded.
**Brace rehearsal.** Ribs down, low back flat to the floor. Same position you want under the bar.
Light, just opening the hips.

sets.name: Squat Warmup — the ROM Ramp (45 → 75), Brace Rehearsal 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 45 for round 1, 75 for round 2, 8 reps each.

**This is where the depth gets set, not where you find out if you have it.** Take both rounds slowly and go deeper than feels necessary — the bottom position you rehearse here is the one you get under 80.

- **Brace before you unrack**, not after
- **Ribs down, pelvis neutral** at the bottom
- Sit between the hips, not back onto the heels

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 45/side round 1, 75/side round 2, 8 reps each.
- **Deeper than feels necessary** — this sets the day's depth
- Brace before the unrack
- Ribs down at the bottom

sets.name: Squat Working (80 × 3 — Depth Is the Job) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 working sets of 6-8, **full depth every rep.**

Stability is banked — last time was the most powerful set of the program and the first time the falling-over feeling was gone entirely. The number holds. **Depth is what improves this week.**

- **Full depth every rep** — if the last two reps of a set shorten up, the set is done at the rep before
- **Slow down into the bottom.** You said your attention moved to depth and tempo on its own; this is that instinct written down
- **Brace before the unrack**, ribs down, pelvis neutral through the bottom
- **Compare against the bodyweight squat from the warmup** — that is the target depth, and closing that gap is the progression
- Nothing near failure. This is a form lift, and the rep where depth shortens is the honest ceiling

**Reflection:** how close did the loaded bottom get to the warmup depth? And did the ankles or the hips run out first?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 80/side, 3 working sets.
- **Full depth every rep** — stop the set when depth shortens
- Slow into the bottom
- Brace before the unrack, ribs down

sets.name: Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine) 🔥
sets.notes: **Both lifts on the same machine — do not leave the station between them.** Leg press runs 4 sets, then the calf raise runs 3 without moving.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side, 4 sets of 12.

**Depth is the load lever here, not plates** — heavier plates shorten the knees-to-chest range that is the whole point of the lift.
- **Knees toward the chest**, as deep as the hips allow without the pelvis tucking
- Controlled down, drive up
- Last set can run near failure — this is a machine, form holds at the limit

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side (already loaded), 3 sets of 15. **Slow eccentric.**
- **Full stretch at the bottom**, full contraction at the top
- Slow down, pause at the stretch
- **Left calf read oddly hard last time** — note whether that repeats

sets.name: 🔆 Knee Flexion — Seated Leg Curl if the Machine Is Fixed, Otherwise Nordic (Spotlight) 🔥
sets.notes:
**Check the seated leg curl first. If it is working, take it — it is the better lift for this week.**

The Nordic has been the knee-flexion slot only because the machine has been broken since W24. Given the choice, the machine wins right now: it loads progressively, it is safe to push near failure, and it does not leave you sore into Friday's lunge-heavy flow the way eccentric-only work does.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — this is the slot that has been missing:**
- **Back seat at position 5.** That setting was a hard-won find — more leverage on the ankle, feels more natural — and seat position moves the numbers on this machine a lot. Pin it before you judge the load
- **Ankles UNDER the pad**, heels driving
- **Slow eccentric is the stimulus.** Judge the top of the ladder by heels driving and no torso lift, not by the stack
- **Pyramid 90 → 100 → 110**, one set each — where you left it before the machine broke
- **Last set can run near failure.** This is a machine and form holds at the limit

**On the single-leg version — worth a look if the machine is free.** You have a documented left-side lag on the upper body (grip on rows and carries, the left palm on dips) and the left calf read oddly hard last week. A single-leg curl is the cleanest read on whether that asymmetry reaches the hamstrings.
- **Run the weaker side first and match reps on the stronger side** — that is the whole point of doing it single-leg
- Roughly half the load, then adjust. **Do not compare the number to the two-leg pyramid** — different pelvis stability, different lift
- **One week of data, not a new prescription.** Log both sides and we will decide whether it earns a permanent slot

**Reflection:** if you ran it single-leg, how far apart were the two sides?

exercises.notes:
**FIRST CHOICE if the machine is fixed.** Back seat at **position 5**. Pyramid **90 → 100 → 110**, one set each.
- **Ankles UNDER the pad**, heels driving
- **Slow eccentric** — that is the stimulus
- Judge the top set by no torso lift, not by the stack
- Last set can run near failure

**Single-leg option:** roughly half the load, **weaker side first, match reps on the stronger.** Log both sides separately — this is a read on asymmetry, not a new prescription.

**FALLBACK if the machine is still broken.** Bodyweight, 3 sets of 5, eccentric only.
- **Heels anchored**, hips extended, glutes squeezed
- **Slowest controlled descent you can manage**
- Catch with the hands, push back up
- Stop the set when the hips start to pike
- **Five reps is the volume** — eccentric-only work makes real soreness and more is not better here

sets.name: Hip Abduction + Adduction (Maintenance Pair) 🔥
sets.notes:
**2 sets each, run as one station pair — they usually sit next to each other.**

Both are maintenance lifts and both are novel stimulus you have said you have not worked before. They stay in rotation.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 210, 2 sets of 15-20. **If it is still as controlled as last time, take the next pin up on set 2 and log it.**
- **Sit tall** — do not lean back to steal range
- Slow eccentric, which is what you picked yourself and preferred
- This is the pelvis-leveling muscle nothing else in the program loads directly

**LOAD:** 290 — top of the stack, 2 sets of 15-20.

There is no load left on this machine, so **tempo is the only lever.**
- Slow and controlled both directions
- **Let the stretch happen at the open position** — that is the part you called good
- Sit tall

sets.name: 🔆 Incline RDL — Fewer Reps, Slower Eccentric (Spotlight) 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD: ONE 45lb plate, held HIGH** at the collarbones. 3 sets of 10, **3s eccentric.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — turning a stamina lift back into a tempo lift:**
- Last time this read **'stamina hard, not load hard'** — the sets got difficult because they were long, not because the hinge was loaded
- **So the reps come down to 10 and a 3s eccentric goes on.** Same plate, different difficulty
- **Hold height is the progression on this lift**, not plate weight. Hip torque is load × horizontal distance from the hip, so hanging the plate lower changes nothing — hugging it high at the collarbones changes everything
- **Clamp it tight to the chest.** Arms straighter makes it read lighter; that is the giveaway that the plate has drifted away from the torso
- **Hinge, do not squat.** Hips travel back, shins stay near vertical, spine neutral
- **Feel it in the hamstrings, not the low back.** If the low back is the loudest thing, the plate has slipped or the spine has rounded

**Reflection:** with 10 reps and a 3s eccentric, was it load-hard this time instead of stamina-hard?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** ONE 45lb plate at the collarbones. 3 sets of 10, **3s eccentric.**
- **Clamp the plate tight and high**
- Hinge — hips back, shins vertical, spine neutral
- Hamstrings loud, low back quiet

sets.notes: Five minutes, mandatory. Hip and QL biased after a full legs day. Slow breathing throughout.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. QL release after loaded squats.
45s each side. Let the hip settle rather than forcing it.
30s each side.
45s each side.
Slow breathing. End here.

Take the leg curl machine if it works; the Nordic is the fallback, not the preference.
The incline RDL keeps the same plate. The 3s eccentric is the change.
